Part 1

Which layers protect the unit, and what can take several out at once?

Part 1 · the plan

Rings round the process, each with a different job

  1. The six layersfrom the control loop to emergency response
  2. Common causeone failure that disables several rings
  3. The register91 items on the safety P&ID

Step 1 · interactive · the onion

What does each layer do on this unit?

Step 2 · interactive · common cause

Which layers survive a power or DCS failure?

Failure

Layers 1–3 need power, air and a computer. The SIS is still safe on power loss because it de-energises to trip.

Step 3 · the safety P&ID

Every layer is drawn on the same core of the unit

91 items; dashed ones are recommended additions (23), most in containment and emergency response.

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • Six layers sit round the process; each catches what the inner one missed.
  • Power or DCS failure is a common cause for layers 1–3.
  • Relief and people-based layers are the reserve that works without the DCS.
2

Part 2

How does the heater trip system act, and how fast?

Part 2 · the plan

Four SIFs, one action: cut the fuel

  1. Cause and effectevery cause closes both fuel valves
  2. Trip timinga delay filters noise and costs time
  3. Restartreset, purge, trial, run

Step 1 · interactive · UY-105

What does each cause do?

The EMS acts on the fuel only: crude flow, stripping steam and the tower stay with the BPCS and the operator.

Step 2 · interactive · FSL-105A

When does the trip act if a pass loses flow?

trip time$t_{trip} = t_{40} + t_{delay}$

Linear fall from 109.4 m³/h is an illustration. The HAZOP run D1 (valve shut) tripped at 00:10, with the pass outlet already at 490 °C.

Step 3 · restart

A trip is latched: the heater is relit only through the sequence

#StepCondition
1Resetfirst-out read and cause removed
2Purge 120 s5 permissives: SDVs closed, fuel MAN 0 %, passes ≥ 40 m³/h, snuffing steam closed
3Light on gas10 s trial; a failed trial needs a new purge
4RUNflame proven
5Admit oilonly with PDC-111 ≥ 150 kPa

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • Every EMS cause closes SDV-106 and SDV-112 and latches the trip.
  • The delay filters noise but adds seconds of firing without flow.
  • Restart always goes through purge and a single light-off trial.

Part 3

How close may the unit run to a limit, and are the layers truly independent?

Part 3 · the plan

Three bands, seven scenarios, eleven practices

  1. Integrity operating windowssafe, limited time, critical
  2. Independenceone failure must not start and blind
  3. Good practiceswhat is OK, what needs work

Step 1 · interactive · IOW

Is the value safe, on borrowed time, or critical?

Step 2 · interactive · independence check

Can one failure start the scenario and blind its protection?

Step 3 · interactive · 11 practices

Which good practices does the unit already meet?

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • Between the alarm and the critical limit the operator is on borrowed time.
  • A trip that shares the control transmitter is a gap.
  • Five practices are met; independence and relief need work first.

To keep

Key Takeaways

1

Count a layer only if it is independent of the cause and of the others.

2

Make the SIS fail safe: de-energise to trip.

3

Act inside the alarm band; past it, time is limited.

4

Never bypass a trip without a permit, a timer and an alarm.
